title: Scarcity of resources versus shortage of finished goods
boundary: Scarcity is the conflict between limited resources and unlimited wants; a temporary goods shortage is a different market condition.
test: A shop has full shelves but households cannot afford everything they want. Has economic scarcity disappeared? Explain.

title: Employers' association versus trade union
boundary: An employers' association represents employers; a trade union represents workers.
test: Identify which organisation would negotiate for a group of factory owners and which would represent their employees.

title: Collective bargaining versus the organisation conducting it
boundary: Collective bargaining is a negotiation process, not another name for a union.
test: A union exists throughout the year but meets management to negotiate pay in June. Which activity is collective bargaining?

title: Real income versus disposable income
boundary: Disposable income concerns income after deductions; real income concerns purchasing power after allowing for prices.
test: Net pay stays unchanged while prices rise. Which measure falls, and which is unchanged?

title: Average revenue versus marginal revenue
boundary: Average revenue is total revenue per unit sold; marginal revenue is the revenue added by one further sale. Units produced and units sold must also be distinguished.
test: A firm sells ten items for N$500 in total and an eleventh adds N$40. Identify average revenue before the extra sale and the extra sale's marginal revenue.

title: Forward versus backward vertical integration
boundary: Moving towards final customers is forward integration; moving towards input suppliers is backward integration.
test: Compare a furniture maker buying a timber supplier with the same maker buying a retail showroom.

title: Economies versus diseconomies of scale
boundary: Economies lower average cost as scale grows; diseconomies raise it.
test: A doubling of output raises average cost because communication breaks down. Which concept applies, and why?

title: Demand determinants versus supply determinants
boundary: Buyer-side conditions shift demand; producer-side conditions shift supply.
test: Compare a rise in consumers' incomes with a rise in production costs. Which curve changes in each case?

title: Minimum wage versus a low wage
boundary: A minimum wage is a legal wage floor; it is not defined by being lower than current earnings.
test: If the market wage is below a binding legal minimum, identify the permitted wage floor and the potential labour-market imbalance.

title: Price control versus shifting demand or supply
boundary: A binding floor or ceiling fixes price away from equilibrium; it does not itself require either curve to shift.
test: Draw a ceiling below equilibrium on unchanged curves and compare quantity demanded with quantity supplied.

title: Social cost versus external cost
boundary: Social cost includes private and external costs. A third party's uncompensated loss is an external cost component.
test: A producer bears N$80 of costs and neighbours bear N$20. Identify each component and the social total.

title: Using a resource versus necessarily overusing it
boundary: Exploitation can mean productive use; it does not automatically mean wasteful or unsustainable use.
test: Compare harvesting below natural regeneration with harvesting faster than replenishment. Must both be rejected for the same reason?

title: Budget balance versus trade balance
boundary: A budget compares government revenue and spending; trade balance compares exports and imports of goods.
test: Government spending exceeds tax revenue while goods exports exceed imports. Identify the two different balances.

title: Absolute advantage versus comparative advantage
boundary: Absolute advantage compares output from resources; comparative advantage compares opportunity costs.
test: A country is more productive in both goods. Can the other country still have comparative advantage? Use opportunity cost to decide.

title: Balance of trade versus balance of payments
boundary: The goods trade balance is only part of the wider record of international economic transactions.
test: Explain why a cross-border investment cannot be recorded merely as a goods export.

title: Ownership sectors versus stages of production
boundary: Public/private distinguish ownership; primary/secondary/tertiary distinguish activity.
test: Classify a state-owned mine on both axes without treating the labels as alternatives.

title: Price elastic versus price inelastic demand
boundary: An elasticity magnitude greater than one is elastic; below one is inelastic.
test: Classify elasticity magnitudes of 0.4 and 1.8 and state what each implies about relative percentage changes.

title: Perfectly inelastic versus merely inelastic demand
boundary: Perfectly inelastic demand has zero quantity response; ordinary inelastic demand can still change in quantity.
test: A price rises while quantity stays exactly unchanged. Is a small fall in quantity consistent with perfectly inelastic demand?

title: Tariff versus non-tariff trade restriction
boundary: A tariff taxes imports; a quota restricts quantity and an embargo bans specified trade.
test: Which measures remain available when the question explicitly excludes import taxes?

title: Production versus productivity
boundary: Production measures output; productivity measures output relative to inputs.
test: Output doubles while labour input triples. Has production risen, and has labour productivity risen?

title: Fiscal versus monetary policy
boundary: Fiscal policy uses government spending and taxation; monetary policy uses money/credit conditions such as interest rates.
test: Classify a tax cut and an interest-rate cut, then explain how each could affect spending.

title: Natural population change versus total population change
boundary: Natural change depends on births and deaths; total change also includes net migration.
test: Births equal deaths but immigration exceeds emigration. Which population measure changes?

title: Labour versus entrepreneurship
boundary: An employed supervisor supplies labour; entrepreneurship concerns organising resources and bearing business risk.
test: Distinguish a salaried supervisor from the owner who puts capital at risk to start the business.

title: Unit of account versus store of value
boundary: Comparing prices uses money as a unit of account; retaining purchasing power for later uses money as a store of value.
test: Contrast checking two price labels with setting money aside for next month.

title: Occupational versus geographical mobility
boundary: Changing occupation differs from moving location; mobility means ability to move, not inability.
test: Compare retraining locally with moving to a new town to do the same job.

title: A substitute pair versus a brand and its product category
boundary: Substitutes are alternative goods meeting a similar need; a brand is already a member of its product category.
test: Explain why a named brand and the category it belongs to are a weaker substitute pair than two distinct alternatives.

title: Proportional tax rate versus equal tax amount
boundary: A constant percentage can produce different cash tax payments at different incomes.
test: Apply a 10% rate to two different incomes and decide whether the tax amounts must be equal.

title: Public goods versus free goods
boundary: Public goods are identified by non-excludability and non-rivalry; free goods have no opportunity cost at the relevant availability. A zero direct charge proves neither.
test: Does tax-funded provision make a scarce service a free good? Explain the resource cost.

title: GDP versus GNP
boundary: Domestic production and national income from production are not interchangeable; cross-border factor income matters.
test: Explain why income earned on residents' productive assets abroad can change the relationship between the two measures.

title: Structural, seasonal and cyclical unemployment
boundary: Classify the stated cause: a recurring seasonal lull, lasting sector/skill mismatch or economy-wide demand slump. A pandemic alone is not a universal classification rule.
test: Compare an annual off-season closure, permanently obsolete skills and a broad recession. Explain why the mechanism determines the label.

title: Transfer earnings versus economic rent
boundary: Transfer earnings are the minimum needed to retain a factor in its present use; economic rent is the excess above that minimum.
test: Actual earnings are N$900 and the minimum acceptable reward is N$700. Allocate both components.

title: Central bank versus commercial bank
boundary: Central-bank monetary and banking-system functions differ from ordinary customer banking services.
test: Distinguish issuing currency and acting as lender of last resort from providing a household current account.

title: Financial investment flows versus current-account trade flows
boundary: Purchasing a business is an investment flow; selling tourism services to non-residents is a service export. Keep legacy capital-account terminology distinct from service receipts.
test: Classify a foreign visitor paying for accommodation and a foreign investor buying the accommodation business.

title: Real income versus real income per head
boundary: Price adjustment and population adjustment do different jobs; total GDP alone does not establish living standards per person.
test: Real output rises while population rises faster. Can real output per head fall?

title: Demand shifts versus price elasticity determinants
boundary: A reason demand increases is different from a reason quantity is more responsive to a price change.
test: Contrast an income rise shifting demand with plentiful substitutes making demand more price elastic.

title: Economic investment versus a financial deposit
boundary: In the production context, investment adds capital goods; placing existing money in an account is a financial transaction.
test: Contrast purchasing a new machine with moving money between two savings accounts.

title: Economic growth versus population growth
boundary: Economic growth concerns increased real output, not merely more inhabitants.
test: If population rises while real output is unchanged, has economic growth necessarily occurred?
